text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government acts on King Hussein's instructions for general amnesty to bread rioters and other prisoners. It decides to form a committee to study around 1,200 cases which may be pardoned.
- Bread prices to be lowered by the beginning of next year by 10 percent.
- Ministers welcome U.S. special status for Jordan as non-NATO ally. Say it is an important step to modernising Jordan's armed forces.
- Foreign Ministry sources say theft was the most likely motive in the murder of Jordan's embassy driver in Iraq last week.
- Commitment to supporting Palestinians is a principle of the Hashemite rule, Prime Minister Kabariti tells audience at Palestinian refugee camp.
- Doctors insist their demands for pay bonuses have not been met in the memorandum of understanding with the health ministry.
- King Hussein, in a meeting with PLO official Mahmoud Abbas, affirms the need to overcome obstacles hindering implementation of the peace process.
- Twenty-one Jordanian prisoners in Israel's Ashqelon prison complain of poor conditions and threaten a hunger strike if they are not released.
- Kabariti says will rectifiy the issue of permanent and termporary passports for Palestinians in refugee camps. Says the right of citizenship and nationality is a human right.
- Trade and Industry Minister Abu al-Ragheb says in Cairo he supports an Arab Free Trade Zone.
- Supply Minister Sobar says ministry study shows Jordan could cut bread prices by 10 percent next year.
- Kabariti says Israel is seeking delays in implementing Oslo agreements to consolidate its occupation in the West Bank.
- Syrian Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Yassin says economic relations with Jordan improving and trade is on the up.
